correctness.rationale: For A=[[0,1],[0,-a]], H=(a,1) and v(s)=exp(As)B, direct exponentiation gives Hv(s)=1. Gaussian conditioning a positive quadrature covariance sum w_i v_i v_i^T with H therefore returns exactly κ² weighted variance of (1-e^{-as})/a, establishing P1=0 for any node and Pm>0 for positive distinct nodes m>=2. Explicit two-point Gauss rule gives κ²h a^{-2}e^{-ah}sinh²(ah/(2√3)). At fixed m>=2, smallest positive Gauss node determines exponential stiffness decay while the continuous integral variance is κ²/(2a³)(1+o(1)). Rank-one induction gives zero filtered covariance at EVERY mesh point from zero initial covariance and noiseless EKL H. For forced y’=-ay+t, y(0)=0, the midpoint conditional mean h(1-e^{-ah/2})/a exceeds exact h/a-(1-e^{-ah})/a² by e^{-ah/2}(2sinh(ah/2)-ah)/a²>0. Independent Gauss-quadrature numerical checks for m=1,2,3,5 and three positive (a,h) pairs verify finite formulas but do not prove limit.
